name: Dice an onion quickly
blurb: The single most repeated task in a kitchen. The standard method uses the onion’s own layers as a grid, so you make three sets of cuts and never chase pieces around the board.
gear: Onions — a whole bag of practice
steps: Cut off the stem end, halve the onion through the root, and peel each half, leaving the root intact.
Place a half flat-side down and make horizontal cuts towards the root, stopping short of it.
Make vertical cuts following the natural radial lines, again stopping short of the root.
Slice across to release perfect dice, adjusting spacing for fine or coarse.
Discard the root, which has been holding the whole thing together.
Practise until you can do it in under a minute, without looking down at your fingers.
tips: The root holds the onion together. Cutting through it early is why beginners end up with a pile of slippery arcs.
A sharp knife ruptures fewer cells, which means significantly fewer tears.
proof: An evenly diced onion in under 60 seconds with no stragglers on the board.
